name: ecoli_structural
description: baseline whole-cell E. coli model plus a parsimony 3D structural packing step (EcoliPackStep) that writes snapshot packs at declared simulation times.

match_simdata.description: Optional path to a REFERENCE vEcoli simData.cPickle (e.g. from a paired comparison run). When set, this composite's initial bulk molecule counts are overlaid from that reference's genuine-vEcoli pre-run state, so a candidate/reference pair driven from the same simData start from an identical t=0 — the same matched-initial-state mechanism scripts/run_comparison_ensemble.py applies via --match-vecoli-simdata/--match-initial-state, expressed declaratively. Default None/empty leaves the baseline's own cached initial state untouched.

match_condition.description: vEcoli growth condition to build the REFERENCE engine under when resolving match_simdata's overlay (matches build_vivarium_ecoli's own condition param). Only consulted when match_simdata is set. A paired comparison must pass the SAME condition its config drives on both engines -- e.g. a with_aa config's candidate must set match_condition='with_aa', not the default 'basal', or the overlay is drawn from the wrong reference condition. Default 'basal' for back-compat with match_simdata callers that predate per-config condition threading (Task 4).

transcript_initiation_mode.description: Phase-2 jump-process opt-in for transcription initiation. 'discrete' (default, legacy): multinomial event distribution with exact Σ N_i = n_target. 'poisson': per-promoter Poisson(n_target · p_i) tau-leap.

polypeptide_initiation_mode.description: Phase-2 jump-process opt-in for translation initiation. Same dispatch as transcript_initiation_mode but for PolypeptideInitiation; ribosome activation per protein becomes per-protein Poisson(n_target · p_i) tau-leap instead of one global multinomial draw.

knockouts.description: Genes to knock out at the translation level — EcoCyc gene ids (EG10526) or monomer ids (LACY-MONOMER[c]). Each named gene's translation efficiency is zeroed on the cached polypeptide-initiation config, so no protein is made — a functional knockout with no ParCa re-fit. Empty = plain baseline. See v2ecoli.perturbations.

media.description: Initial growth medium — any condition in the cache's saved_media (e.g. 'minimal_plus_amino_acids', 'minimal_succinate', 'minimal_minus_oxygen'). Sets the environment's initial media_id so media_update shifts the cell onto that condition on the first tick and metabolism responds (e.g. amino-acid-rich media grows faster) — a lightweight media perturbation from the existing cache, no ParCa re-fit. Default 'minimal' = unchanged. For a rigorously-calibrated condition, run a per-condition ParCa cache instead (see showcase-4).

features.description: Opt-in feature-module names to insert in addition to the boolean toggles (e.g. ['mass_conservation']). Each must be a key in FEATURE_MODULES.

ppgpp_regulation.description: Enable ppGpp-mediated regulation of transcription initiation (ppgpp-initiation step). On by default.

trna_attenuation.description: Enable tRNA transcriptional attenuation (trna-attenuation-config step). Off by default.

supercoiling.description: Enable DNA supercoiling dynamics (dna-supercoiling-step + dna_supercoiling_listener). Off by default.

mass_conservation.description: Enable the opt-in runtime mass-conservation check (ecoli-mass-conservation step). Off by default — the residual is not yet calibrated, so it warns each tick.

exchange_fluxes.description: {leaf_name: exchange_key} — re-home named environment.exchange fluxes onto listeners.exchange_flux.<leaf> so the listeners-only XArray view carries them (e.g. {'glucose_exchange': 'GLC[p]'}). Empty = off.

emitter.description: Observation sink. Single-cell: parquet (hive column store, default), sqlite (time-series db), xarray (in-memory arrays), or null (global_time only). Batch (n_seeds>1 / n_generations>1): parquet, xarray (per-lineage zarr), or 'both' (parquet + zarr; what the dashboard per-run charts read). 'both' is batch only; 'sqlite'/'null' are single-cell only.

emitter_out_dir.description: Single-cell observation-sink output directory override. Empty (default) = unchanged behavior: each emitter resolves its own default location (parquet -> workspace .pbg/parquet-runs, sqlite -> workspace .pbg or out/, xarray -> workspace .pbg/xarray-runs or out/xarray). Set this to pin the sink to an explicit directory instead — e.g. a standalone/provisioned run with no workspace on disk (a generic runner building this composite via core_extensions alone, with no dashboard around it). Ignored for emitter='null'. Batch runs use the separate out_dir param instead.

injected_processes.description: Fork process-injection spec {fork_repo, add_processes, swap_processes, process_configs, topology, time_step}; empty = none.

n_seeds.description: Number of independent seeds to run (vEcoli's n_init_sims); seeds are seed .. seed+n_seeds-1. 1 = a single cell (default). >1 launches a batch run.

n_generations.description: Cell-division generations to follow per seed lineage. >1 (or n_seeds>1) launches a batch run.

single_daughters.description: Batch runs only: follow ONE daughter per division (vEcoli's default). Off = binary-tree lineage.

time_step.description: Batch runs only: simulation time step in seconds.

max_duration.description: Batch runs only: per-generation sim-time cap (seconds).

variants.description: Batch runs only: vEcoli-style variant grid ({name: {target, value}}) crossed with the seed range.

out_dir.description: Explicit pack out_dir override; when unset, derived from workspace.yaml's layout.studies as '<studies_root>/<study>/viz/3d'.

experiment_id.description: Batch runs only: id stamped into the parquet partitions and zarr store names.

analyses.description: Batch runs only: 'applicable' runs every ported analysis at the scales this batch covers; 'none' skips.

study.description: Study slug; used to derive the default pack out_dir.

parallel.description: Batch runs only: 'ray' to fan out across worker processes; '' for sequential.

initial_carry_state_path.description: Batch runs only, per-generation checkpoint/resume (backlog item 34): path to a prior generation's saved daughter state, threaded to every branch's LineageProcess. Empty = fresh lineage at generation 0 (default, unchanged single-invocation behavior). Set together with initial_generation_index by a wave orchestrator resuming a checkpointed lineage.

initial_generation_index.description: Batch runs only, per-generation checkpoint/resume: the generation index this invocation resumes at. Must be 0 when initial_carry_state_path is empty (enforced by LineageProcess at run time).

daughter_state_out_path.description: Batch runs only, per-generation checkpoint/resume: path to persist this invocation's daughter state to, for the next generation's job to resume from. Empty = no checkpoint hand-off.

top_n.description: Number of top-abundance ingredient species to pack.

relax.description: Relax each ingredient's structure in explicit-water MD (compacts disordered tails) before packing; cached under cache_dir/relaxed. Opt-in; adds significant first-run compute.

relax_params.description: Optional overrides for the relax MD (e.g. {equil_ps: 100.0}); see pbg_openmm.relax_in_water.

envelope.description: Pack into a gram-negative envelope (inner membrane + periplasm + outer membrane), routing molecules by their [compartment] tag. Default on.

ecoli-tf-unbinding.doc:
TfUnbinding — deterministic release of all DNA-bound TFs to the free active pool.

    n_released_j = ∑_i bound_TF[i,j]     (sum over promoters i)
    bound_TF ← 0     (reset promoter occupancy matrix)
    Δmass_i = -∑_j bound_TF[i,j] · m_j   (mass moved promoter submass → bulk)
  bound_TF: promoters × TF species;  m_j: mass (fg) of active TF j.

_contract.summary: Deterministically releases every DNA-bound TF back to the free active bulk pool, zeroes the promoter occupancy matrix, and removes the corresponding TF mass from promoter submass — run before signalling so TFs can re-equilibrate before TfBinding re-binds them.
_contract.description: bound_TF: promoters × TF species;  m_j: mass (fg) of active TF j.

inputs.promoters: reads the bound_TF occupancy matrix (and current submass fields) to count how many of each TF are bound; empty → no-op.
inputs.bulk: provides the free active-TF pool that released TFs are added back to.
inputs.global_time: reads simulation time to decide (with next_update_time) whether this tick fires.
inputs.timestep: reads the tick length to schedule the next update time.
inputs.next_update_time: reads the scheduled fire time gating update_condition.

outputs.bulk: adds n_released_j molecules of each TF j back to the free active pool.
outputs.promoters: resets bound_TF to zero and decrements each promoter's submass fields by the released TF mass.
outputs.next_update_time: writes the next scheduled fire time (global_time + timestep).

config.tf_ids: list of transcription-factor species whose [c] active forms are released.
config.active_tf_masses: per-TF active-molecule mass m_j (fg) removed from promoter submass on release.
config.submass_indices: maps promoter submass fields to columns of the released-mass matrix.

math: n_released_j = ∑_i bound_TF[i,j]     (sum over promoters i)
bound_TF ← 0     (reset promoter occupancy matrix)
Δmass_i = -∑_j bound_TF[i,j] · m_j   (mass moved promoter submass → bulk)

symbols.n_released_j: count of TF j molecules released from DNA to the free active pool
symbols.bound_TF[i,j]: 1 if TF j is bound at promoter i, else 0 (indicator)
symbols.\u0394mass_i: mass removed from promoter i submass on release (fg)
symbols.m_j: mass of one active TF j molecule (fg)

assumptions: Release is deterministic and total: every bound TF is freed each time the process fires.
TF mass is conserved — it moves from promoter submass back to the bulk active pool.

ecoli-equilibrium.doc:
Equilibrium — ligand–TF binding driven to steady state.

1. ODE solve for integer reaction fluxes ν:  x_ss, ν = fluxesAndMoleculesToSS(x, V, N_A).
2. Greedy correction under allocation: while any(S·ν + x_alloc < 0),
   decrement offending forward/reverse fluxes (clamp ≥ 0).
Δx = S·ν;  S = stoichiometry matrix (molecules × reactions).

_contract.summary: Bind/unbind ligands to their transcription-factor partners by solving the reaction system to steady state each step, rounding the continuous solution to integer reaction fluxes, and greedily correcting those fluxes so no allocated metabolite goes negative.
_contract.description: 2. Greedy correction under allocation: while any(S·ν + x_alloc < 0),

inputs.bulk: Reads counts x of the equilibrium molecules (ligands, TFs, complexes) as the ODE initial condition and as the non-negativity bound in the greedy correction.
inputs.listeners: Reads listeners.mass.cell_mass and divides by cell_density to get the volume V used to convert counts to concentrations for the ODE.
inputs.timestep: Reads dt: the kinetic-phase integration horizon and the divisor for the reaction_rates listener.
inputs.DnaA_boxes: Optional read-only port: counts DnaA-box rows in the bound-ATP form to add extra DNAA-INTRINSIC-HYDROLYSIS-RXN flux covering the bound pool (empty ⇒ free-pool-only behaviour).
inputs.dnaa_hydrolysis: Optional port carrying dnaa_box_binding's bound-hydrolysis event count so byproducts are sampled from the same event; a -1 sentinel means unwired and the step resamples locally.

outputs.bulk: Writes Δx = S·ν, the net binding/unbinding change per molecule, with the bound-pool DnaA-ATP/ADP portion reverted (bound ATP/ADP are box-bound, not in bulk).
outputs.listeners: Writes equilibrium_listener.reaction_rates: the per-product molecule change divided by the timestep (1/s).

config.stoichMatrix: Stoichiometry matrix S (molecules × reactions) mapping fluxes ν to count changes Δx.
config.moleculeNames: Bulk ids of the equilibrium species, in the row order of S.
config.reaction_ids: Reaction ids in the column order of S (used to locate the DnaA hydrolysis reaction).
config.complex_ids: Bulk ids of the TF–ligand complex products formed by binding (stored at init; unused in this build's update path).
config.cell_density: Cell density dividing cell_mass to obtain the volume V for count↔concentration conversion.
config.n_avogadro: Avogadro's number N_A converting between counts and molar concentrations.
config.fluxesAndMoleculesToSS: Legacy opaque solver returning steady-state counts and fluxes when rates_fn is absent.
config.rates_fn: Inline ODE rate function r(t, y, kf, kr); if provided it supersedes fluxesAndMoleculesToSS.
config.rates_jac_fn: Jacobian of rates_fn for the stiff solver.
config.rates_fwd: Forward rate constants kf per reaction.
config.rates_rev: Reverse rate constants kr per reaction.
config.mets_to_rxn_fluxes: Matrix mapping continuous molecule-count deltas back to reaction fluxes ν.
config.Rp: Reactant partition matrix: molecules consumed by forward fluxes.
config.Pp: Product partition matrix: molecules consumed by reverse fluxes.

math: 1. ODE solve for integer reaction fluxes ν:  x_ss, ν = fluxesAndMoleculesToSS(x, V, N_A).
decrement offending forward/reverse fluxes (clamp ≥ 0).
Δx = S·ν;  S = stoichiometry matrix (molecules × reactions).

symbols.x: vector of current molecule counts for the equilibrium species (counts)
symbols.x_ss: steady-state molecule counts returned by the ODE solve (counts)
symbols.x_alloc: molecule counts actually allocated to this process for the greedy check (counts)
symbols.V: cell volume, computed as cell_mass / cell_density (litres, L)
symbols.\u03bd: integer reaction-flux vector: net number of times each reaction fires (counts)
symbols.\u0394x: net molecule-count change applied to bulk this step, Δx = S·ν (counts)

assumptions: Ligands are TF-specific and not consumed by other processes, so this runs as a plain Step with no request/allocate/evolve cycle.
Fast reactions reach equilibrium within a step (steady-state solve to t≈1e20); reactions flagged in integrate_dt_mask are instead integrated over dt in a kinetic phase.
Continuous ODE concentration changes are converted to counts and stochastically rounded to integer fluxes ν.
The greedy correction decrements offending forward/reverse fluxes one unit at a time (clamped at 0) until no allocated metabolite is negative, terminating within sum(|ν|) iterations.
The DnaA bound-pool hydrolysis extension is a no-op when its ids are absent from the cache or no DnaA boxes are bound, collapsing to free-pool-only flux.
references: Sekimizu (1987) — DnaA intrinsic ATP-hydrolysis rate (~0.046/min) used for the bound-pool hydrolysis flux.

ecoli-two-component-system.doc:
TwoComponentSystem — phosphotransfer signaling kinetics (ODE integration).

Solve molecule-count ODEs over the timestep:
    dx/dt = f(x);   integrate t: 0→dt (scipy solve_ivp, BDF);   Δx = x(dt) − x(0).
Under-allocation: re-solve to long-horizon steady state (10000 s), extract
this timestep's Δx to stay physically consistent with reduced counts.
x: counts of histidine kinases, response regulators, and their phospho-forms.

_contract.summary: Phosphotransfer signaling: integrate the ODE system for histidine kinase / response-regulator phosphorylation over the timestep and apply the net molecule-count changes. Runs as a plain Step (its molecules are process-private, so no allocator competition).
_contract.description:
Solve molecule-count ODEs over the timestep:
Under-allocation: re-solve to long-horizon steady state (10000 s), extract
this timestep's Δx to stay physically consistent with reduced counts.
x: counts of histidine kinases, response regulators, and their phospho-forms.

inputs.bulk: Reads counts of histidine kinases, response regulators, and their phospho-forms → initial ODE concentrations; writes back integer net count changes Δx.
inputs.listeners: Reads mass.cell_mass to compute cell volume for the counts↔concentration conversion.
inputs.timestep: Sets the integration horizon dt for the ODE solve.

outputs.bulk: Writes the net phosphotransfer count changes Δx (rounded to int) across all tracked molecules.

config.moleculeNames: Molecule species (histidine kinases, response regulators, phospho-forms) tracked by the ODE.
config.cell_density: Cell density (g/L) → cell volume for the counts↔concentration conversion.
config.rates_fn: Reaction-rate law r(y,t) forming the ODE RHS dy/dt = S_full·r(y).
config.rates_jac_fn: Analytic Jacobian of the rate law, supplied to the stiff BDF/Radau solver.
config.dependency_matrix: Maps independent-molecule changes to changes for all molecules.
config.independent_molecule_indexes: Indices of the independent molecules integrated directly.
config.atp_reaction_reactant_mask: Mask of ATP-reactant molecules used to cap phosphorylation by available ATP.
config.independent_molecules_atp_index: Index of ATP within the independent molecules for the availability cap.

math: counts→conc: y = x /(V·N_A);   dy/dt = S_full · r(y);   Δx = (y(dt) − y(0))·V·N_A

symbols.x: molecule counts of histidine kinases, response regulators, and phospho-forms (count)
symbols.dx/dt: time derivative of the molecule state
symbols.f(x): phosphotransfer reaction rate law (net RHS of the ODE)
symbols.\u0394x: net count change applied over the timestep (count)

assumptions: Phosphotransfer molecules are process-private (no resource competition), so the process runs as a plain Step.
The stiff ODE is solved with solve_ivp, trying LSODA/BDF/Radau/RK45/RK23/DOP853 and halving the horizon if concentrations go negative.
ATP-consuming phosphorylation is capped by the minimum available ATP-reactant count.
On under-allocation (required counts > available), the system is re-solved to a 10000 s steady state and this step's Δx is extracted for physical consistency.

ecoli-rna-maturation.doc:
RNA Maturation — stoichiometric processing of unprocessed tRNA/rRNA into mature forms.

    reaction_off = (E · enzyme_present) < n_required;   n_unproc[off] = 0
    n_mature = S · n_unproc;   ppi = ppi_per_rxn · n_unproc  (PPi consumed, added to 5' ends)
    rRNA variant consolidation: Δnts = Δnt_countsᵀ · n_variant;  NMP +Δ, H2O −Σ, H⁺ +Σ
  S: stoich (mature × unprocessed, CSR); E: enzyme-requirement (rxns × enzymes);
  Δnt_counts: NMP difference variant vs canonical 16S/23S/5S.

_contract.summary: Stoichiometrically converts unprocessed tRNA/rRNA into mature forms (n_mature = S·n_unproc) gated by maturation-enzyme availability, and consolidates the genomic 16S/23S/5S rRNA variants onto their single canonical species with NMP/H2O mass balance.
_contract.description:
S: stoich (mature × unprocessed, CSR); E: enzyme-requirement (rxns × enzymes);
Δnt_counts: NMP difference variant vs canonical 16S/23S/5S.

inputs.bulk: reads counts of unprocessed RNAs, the maturation enzymes (to gate reactions), and the 16S/23S/5S rRNA variants to consolidate
inputs.bulk_total: declared port aliased to the same ('bulk',) store as `bulk`; present in inputs()/topology for framework symmetry, but update() reads the full unpartitioned counts through the `bulk` port, not this one

outputs.bulk: produces mature RNAs (+S·n_unproc), consumes unprocessed RNAs, consumes PPi (−ppi_update; added onto the mature-RNA 5' ends), moves each rRNA variant onto its canonical species, and adds/removes NMPs with balancing H2O (−) and H⁺ (+)
outputs.listeners: writes rna_maturation_listener: total_maturation_events, total_degraded_ntps, per-species unprocessed_rnas_consumed, mature_rnas_generated, and maturation_enzyme_counts

config.n_required_enzymes: minimum enzyme counts per reaction; reactions with (E·enzyme_present) below this are turned off
config.n_ppi_added: PPi consumed (added onto the 5' ends) per maturation reaction
config.degraded_nt_counts: nucleotide fragments released per unprocessed RNA (contributes to added bases / degraded ntps)
config.delta_nt_counts_16s: NMP difference between each 16S variant and the canonical 16S
config.delta_nt_counts_23s: NMP difference between each 23S variant and the canonical 23S
config.delta_nt_counts_5s: NMP difference between each 5S variant and the canonical 5S
config.variant_16s_rRNA_ids: bulk ids of 16S rRNA variants consolidated onto main_16s_rRNA_id
config.variant_23s_rRNA_ids: bulk ids of 23S rRNA variants consolidated onto main_23s_rRNA_id
config.variant_5s_rRNA_ids: bulk ids of 5S rRNA variants consolidated onto main_5s_rRNA_id
config.main_16s_rRNA_id: canonical 16S species receiving consolidated variant counts
config.main_23s_rRNA_id: canonical 23S species receiving consolidated variant counts
config.main_5s_rRNA_id: canonical 5S species receiving consolidated variant counts
config.unprocessed_rna_ids: bulk ids of the unprocessed RNAs consumed
config.mature_rna_ids: bulk ids of the mature RNAs produced
config.rna_maturation_enzyme_ids: bulk ids of the maturation enzymes gating reactions

math: reaction_off = (E · enzyme_present) < n_required;   n_unproc[off] = 0
n_mature = S · n_unproc;   ppi = ppi_per_rxn · n_unproc  (PPi consumed, added to 5' ends)
rRNA variant consolidation: Δnts = Δnt_countsᵀ · n_variant;  NMP +Δ, H2O −Σ, H⁺ +Σ

symbols.enzyme_present: boolean vector of maturation enzymes with nonzero count
symbols.n_required: minimum enzyme count required per maturation reaction (count)
symbols.n_unproc: counts of unprocessed RNA per reaction (count); zeroed where reaction is off
symbols.n_mature: counts of mature RNA produced = S·n_unproc (count)
symbols.ppi: pyrophosphate consumed — added onto the 5' ends of the mature RNAs per maturation reaction (count)
symbols.ppi_per_rxn: PPi consumed (incorporated) per unprocessed RNA reaction (count)
symbols.n_variant: copy counts of a genomic rRNA variant being consolidated (count)
symbols.\u0394nt_counts: NMP nucleotide-count difference, variant vs canonical 16S/23S/5S (nt)
symbols.\u0394nts: net NMPs added on consolidation = Δnt_countsᵀ·n_variant (nt)
symbols.NMP: free nucleotide monophosphates added/removed for mass balance (count)

assumptions: Water and NMPs consumed are marginal relative to their pools, so there is no cross-process resource competition — it runs as a plain Step reading full bulk counts.
A maturation reaction proceeds only if all its required enzymes are present at or above n_required.
rRNA variant sequences differ from the canonical only in nucleotide composition; the difference is balanced by adding/removing NMPs, consuming H2O and releasing H⁺.

ecoli-tf-binding.doc:
TfBinding — stochastic occupancy of promoter sites by transcription factors.

    p_bound_j = p_promoter_bound_tf(n_active_j, n_inactive_j)   (1.0 for 0CS TFs)
    n_to_bind_j = min(∑ StochasticRound(p_bound_j, N_j), n_available_TF_j)
  then n_to_bind_j promoter sites are chosen uniformly at random and bound.
    Δmass_i = ∑_j ΔTF[i,j] · m_j     (mass moved bulk → promoter submass)
  N_j: available promoter sites for TF j;  m_j: mass (fg) of active TF j.
  MarA (PD00365): n_active = 34 · [marR-tet]/([marR]+[marR-tet]).

_contract.summary: Recomputes promoter occupancy each tick: releases all currently bound TFs, computes a per-TF binding probability, then stochastically re-binds a limited number of promoter sites and moves the TF mass onto them.
_contract.description:
then n_to_bind_j promoter sites are chosen uniformly at random and bound.
N_j: available promoter sites for TF j;  m_j: mass (fg) of active TF j.

inputs.promoters: reads each promoter's TU_index and bound_TF to know current occupancy and which promoters each TF may bind; an empty promoter set short-circuits the tick.
inputs.bulk: reads free active-TF counts (per TF species) that, together with released bound TFs, bound the number of promoters that can be occupied.
inputs.bulk_total: reads total active/inactive TF counts (and marR / marR-tet counts for MarA) used to evaluate the binding-probability function.
inputs.listeners: declared so the process can overwrite-merge into the rna_synth_prob listener group; no listener value is read by update (write-only port).
inputs.global_time: reads simulation time to decide (with next_update_time) whether this tick fires.
inputs.timestep: reads the tick length to schedule the next update time.
inputs.next_update_time: reads the scheduled fire time gating update_condition.

outputs.bulk: returns every bound TF to the free active pool, then decrements it again by the number of promoters each TF newly binds.
outputs.promoters: sets the recomputed bound_TF occupancy matrix and updates each promoter's submass fields by the net TF mass bound/released.
outputs.listeners: writes p_promoter_bound, n_promoter_bound, n_actual_bound, n_available_promoters (and optionally the heavy n_bound_TF_per_TU matrix).
outputs.next_update_time: writes the next scheduled fire time (global_time + timestep).

config.tf_ids: list of transcription-factor species handled; sets n_TF.
config.tf_to_tf_type: per-TF regulatory type ('0CS' always-bound, '1CS', '2CS') selecting how p_bound is computed.
config.p_promoter_bound_tf: fitted function mapping active/inactive TF counts to the single-promoter binding probability p_bound_j.
config.delta_prob: sparse TF-effect matrix (deltaI/deltaJ/shape) used to derive which TUs each TF regulates and n_TU.
config.active_to_bound: maps a 1CS TF to its DNA-bound form for locating the inactive-TF species.
config.active_to_inactive_tf: maps a 2CS TF to its unphosphorylated (inactive) species.
config.get_unbound: resolves the unbound species id for a self-binding 1CS TF.
config.bulk_mass_data: per-molecule masses used to build each active TF's mass (fg) moved on binding.
config.bulk_molecule_ids: bulk id list used to locate each TF's mass entry.
config.submass_indices: maps promoter submass fields to columns of the TF mass matrix.
config.n_avogadro: Avogadro constant for the count→mass conversion of TF masses.
config.emit_n_bound_TF_per_TU: toggles the heavy per-TU×per-TF binding-count listener (~900 KB/tick).

math: p_bound_j = p_promoter_bound_tf(n_active_j, n_inactive_j)   (1.0 for 0CS TFs)
n_to_bind_j = min(∑ StochasticRound(p_bound_j, N_j), n_available_TF_j)
Δmass_i = ∑_j ΔTF[i,j] · m_j     (mass moved bulk → promoter submass)
MarA (PD00365): n_active = 34 · [marR-tet]/([marR]+[marR-tet]).

symbols.p_bound_j: probability a single promoter site is occupied by TF j (dimensionless, 0–1)
symbols.n_to_bind_j: number of promoter sites TF j should occupy this tick (count)
symbols.N_j: number of available promoter sites for TF j (count)
symbols.n_available_TF_j: number of free+released TF j molecules available to bind (count)
symbols.\u0394mass_i: net TF mass transferred to/from promoter i submass (fg)
symbols.\u0394TF[i,j]: change in bound-state of TF j at promoter i (+1 bind / −1 release)
symbols.m_j: mass of one active TF j molecule (fg)

assumptions: All DNA-bound TFs are first released to the free active pool each tick, then binding is recomputed from scratch.
0CS (constitutive) TFs bind with probability 1; 1CS/2CS TFs use the fitted p_promoter_bound_tf on their active vs inactive counts.
Per-promoter binding is a Bernoulli trial (via stochastic rounding); the number actually bound is capped by the available TF molecules.
Which promoter sites are occupied is chosen uniformly at random among the TF's regulated promoters.
MarA (PD00365) active count is set to 34·[marR-tet]/([marR]+[marR-tet]), reflecting tetracycline de-repression of marRAB.

Placed after all Steps of each execution layer (see :ref:`partitioning`)
to ensure that unique molecules are completely up-to-date

_contract.summary: type(object) -> the object's type
_contract.description: type(name, bases, dict, **kwds) -> a new type

ecoli-protein-degradation.doc:
Protein Degradation — first-order Poisson hydrolysis of protein monomers.

    nᵢ_deg ~ min(Poisson(kᵢ · dt · nᵢ), nᵢ)
    Δmetabolites = S · n_deg
    Proteinᵢ + (Lᵢ−1) H2O → ∑ⱼ aᵢⱼ · AAⱼ
  kᵢ: first-order degradation rate (1/s); nᵢ: copies of protein i;
  aᵢⱼ: count of AA j per protein i; Lᵢ = ∑ⱼ aᵢⱼ (residues);
  S: stoichiometry (metabolites × proteins), +AA release, −(Lᵢ−1) H2O.

_contract.summary: First-order Poisson hydrolysis of protein monomers: each step draw the number of copies of each protein that degrade, then apply the stoichiometric release of amino acids and consumption of water. Single-pass Step (no resource competition, no request/allocate cycle).
_contract.description:
kᵢ: first-order degradation rate (1/s); nᵢ: copies of protein i;
S: stoichiometry (metabolites × proteins), +AA release, −(Lᵢ−1) H2O.

inputs.bulk: Reads current protein counts nᵢ to draw Poisson degradation counts; writes back −nᵢ_deg proteins, +released amino acids, and −(Lᵢ−1)·nᵢ_deg water via the stoichiometry matrix.
inputs.timestep: Provides dt scaling the per-protein Poisson degradation rate.

outputs.bulk: Writes the stoichiometric metabolite deltas (amino-acid release, water consumption) and the per-protein count decrements.

config.raw_degradation_rate: Per-protein first-order degradation rate constants kᵢ (1/s).
config.protein_lengths: Vestigial: read into self.protein_lengths but never used in update(). Water consumed per hydrolysis is NOT set from this — the −(Lᵢ−1) H2O row is derived from amino_acid_counts as −(Σⱼ aᵢⱼ − 1), i.e. Lᵢ = Σⱼ aᵢⱼ.
config.amino_acid_counts: Amino-acid composition matrix aᵢⱼ (AA j per protein i); forms the AA-release rows of S.
config.protein_ids: Protein species identities, defining the columns of the stoichiometry matrix.
config.amino_acid_ids: Amino-acid species identities, defining the AA rows of the stoichiometry matrix.
config.water_id: Bulk id of water, whose row carries the −(Lᵢ−1) peptide-bond-hydrolysis stoichiometry.

math: nᵢ_deg ~ min(Poisson(kᵢ · dt · nᵢ), nᵢ)
Δmetabolites = S · n_deg
Proteinᵢ + (Lᵢ−1) H2O → ∑ⱼ aᵢⱼ · AAⱼ
aᵢⱼ: count of AA j per protein i; Lᵢ = ∑ⱼ aᵢⱼ (residues);

symbols.n\u1d62_deg: copies of protein i degraded this step = min(Poisson(kᵢ·dt·nᵢ), nᵢ) (count)
symbols.k\u1d62: first-order degradation rate constant for protein i (1/s)
symbols.S: degradation stoichiometry, metabolites × proteins (+AA release rows, −(Lᵢ−1) H2O row)
symbols.L\u1d62: length of protein i in residues, = Σⱼ aᵢⱼ
symbols.a\u1d62\u2c7c: count of amino acid j in one copy of protein i
symbols.AA\u2c7c: amino acid species j released on hydrolysis (count)
symbols.H2O: water consumed: (Lᵢ−1) molecules per degraded copy of protein i

assumptions: Degradation is a first-order Poisson process, independent per protein species, capped at the available copy count.
Each degraded chain of length L consumes (L−1) water molecules (N−1 peptide-bond hydrolyses) and releases its constituent amino acids.
Protein complexes and explicit protease mechanisms are not modeled (TODO in source).
Single-pass: no resource competition, so no request/allocate/evolve cycle is used.

ppgpp-initiation.doc:
Compute ppGpp-dependent basal_prob and fracActiveRnap.

Reads ppGpp concentration from bulk, computes synthesis probabilities
using the synth_prob callable, and writes results to ppgpp_state store
for TranscriptInitiation to consume.

_contract.summary: Optional regulator: computes ppGpp-dependent per-TU basal synthesis probabilities and the RNAP active fraction from the current ppGpp concentration, and publishes them to the ppgpp_state store that TranscriptInitiation reads.

inputs.bulk: reads the ppGpp molecule count and converts it to a concentration ppgpp_conc.
inputs.listeners: reads listeners.mass.cell_mass to form the cell volume and the count→molar factor.

outputs.ppgpp_state: writes basal_prob (per-TU ppGpp-dependent synthesis probabilities) and frac_active_rnap for TranscriptInitiation to consume; when absent TranscriptInitiation falls back to media defaults.

config.ppgpp: bulk id of ppGpp whose count sets the regulatory concentration.
config.synth_prob: fitted callable mapping (ppgpp_conc, copy_number) to per-TU basal synthesis probabilities.
config.copy_number: expected gene copy number at the reference doubling time, passed to synth_prob.
config.fraction_active_rnap_bound: active RNAP fraction in the ppGpp-bound limit (frac_active_rnap_bound).
config.fraction_active_rnap_free: active RNAP fraction in the ppGpp-free limit (frac_active_rnap_free).
config.ppgpp_km_squared: squared half-saturation ppGpp concentration km_sq for the RNAP-binding Hill term.
config.get_rnap_active_fraction_from_ppGpp: legacy opaque callable used for the active fraction when the Hill parameters are not supplied.
config.cell_density: cell density used to convert cell_mass to volume.
config.n_avogadro: Avogadro constant for the count→molar conversion.
config.trna_attenuation: whether fitted attenuation adjustments are added to basal_prob for attenuated TUs.
config.attenuated_rna_indices: TU indices receiving the attenuation adjustment when trna_attenuation is on.
config.attenuation_adjustments: additive basal_prob adjustments applied at the attenuated TU indices.

math: ppgpp_conc = ppGpp_count / (n_avogadro · cell_volume);  cell_volume = cell_mass / cell_density
basal_prob = synth_prob(ppgpp_conc, copy_number)
f_bound = ppgpp_conc² / (km_sq + ppgpp_conc²)
frac_active_rnap = f_bound · frac_active_rnap_bound + (1 − f_bound) · frac_active_rnap_free

symbols.ppgpp_conc: ppGpp concentration derived from its bulk count (converted to µmol/L for the Hill term)
symbols.copy_number: expected gene copy number at the reference doubling time (dimensionless)
symbols.f_bound: fraction of RNAP in the ppGpp-bound state (dimensionless, 0–1)
symbols.km_sq: squared half-saturation ppGpp concentration for RNAP binding ((µmol/L)²)
symbols.frac_active_rnap: resulting active RNAP fraction published to ppgpp_state (dimensionless, 0–1)
symbols.frac_active_rnap_bound: active RNAP fraction in the fully ppGpp-bound limit (dimensionless)
symbols.frac_active_rnap_free: active RNAP fraction in the ppGpp-free limit (dimensionless)
symbols.cell_mass: cell mass used to form the volume (fg)
symbols.cell_density: cell density used in the volume conversion (g/L)

assumptions: ppGpp concentration is computed from its bulk count and the cell volume (cell_mass / cell_density).
The RNAP active fraction follows a Hill relation in ppGpp (exponent 2) interpolating between the free and bound limiting fractions; a legacy callable is used when Hill parameters are absent.
When tRNA attenuation is enabled, fixed adjustments are added to the basal probabilities of the attenuated TUs.

ecoli-complexation.doc:
Complexation — spontaneous monomer→complex assembly (Gillespie SSA).

Continuous-time Markov chain over reactions (stoichiometry S, rows=reactions, rates k):
    x(t+dt) = StochasticSystem.evolve(dt, x(t), k)
    propensity a_j = k_j · ∏_i C(x_i, |S_ji|);   Δx = outcome − x(t) = Sᵀ·occurrences.
Reactants are complex-specific (no shared-resource competition).

_contract.summary: Assembles monomers into macromolecular complexes via a single Gillespie SSA (StochasticSystem) run over the whole timestep, using a stoichiometry matrix S and per-reaction rate constants k.
_contract.description: Reactants are complex-specific (no shared-resource competition).

inputs.bulk: reads the counts of the monomer/complex molecules that participate in complexation reactions; these are the SSA state vector x(t)
inputs.timestep: SSA integration interval dt (s) passed to StochasticSystem.evolve

outputs.bulk: applies the net count change Δx = x(t+dt) − x(t): consumes reactant monomers and produces complexes
outputs.listeners: writes complexation_listener.complexation_events — the per-reaction occurrence counts from the SSA run

config.stoichiometry: stoichiometry matrix S (reactions × molecules) defining each complexation reaction
config.molecule_names: bulk ids of the molecules indexed by S (maps SSA state to bulk positions)
config.reaction_ids: identifiers of the complexation reactions (columns/rows of S)
config.complex_ids: identifiers of the assembled complex products

math: Continuous-time Markov chain over reactions (stoichiometry S, rows=reactions, rates k):
x(t+dt) = StochasticSystem.evolve(dt, x(t), k)
propensity a_j = k_j · ∏_i C(x_i, |S_ji|);   Δx = outcome − x(t) = Sᵀ·occurrences.

symbols.S: stoichiometry matrix, reactions × molecules (stochastic_arrow convention: row j is reaction j, column i is molecule i)
symbols.k: vector of per-reaction propensity rate constants k_j (1/s)
symbols.S_ji: stoichiometric coefficient of molecule i in reaction j (entry at row j, column i of S)
symbols.a_j: propensity of reaction j = k_j·∏_i C(x_i, |S_ji|) (1/s)
symbols.dt: timestep over which the SSA is integrated (s)
symbols.occurrences: number of times each reaction fired over dt (count)
symbols.\u0394x: net molecule-count change = outcome − x(t) = Sᵀ·occurrences (count); computed directly from evolve's outcome, not a literal matrix product

assumptions: Complexes form spontaneously and complexation reactions are fast, completing within one timestep.
Each complex's reactants are complex-specific, so there is no shared-resource competition — a single Gillespie call suffices and it runs as a plain Step.
Complex dissociation and shuffling are not modeled here.

ecoli-chromosome-replication.doc:
Chromosome Replication — initiate, elongate, and terminate replication forks.

1. Initiation: fire when  M_cell / n_oriC ≥ M_critical(τ);  +2 replisomes·oriC, +2 domains.
2. Elongation: seqs = buildSequences(template, pos, ν·dt); polymerize(seqs, dNTPs, limit);
   Δm_DNA = ∑ᵢ (elongated_ntᵢ · weightᵢ);  PPi released = dNTP polymerized.
3. Termination: fork ends when |coordinate| = L_replichore; domain splits, subunits recycled.
  M_cell: cell mass (fg); n_oriC: oriC count; M_critical(τ): mass/oriC threshold at doubling time τ;
  ν: stochastic elongation rate (nt/s); dt: timestep; L_replichore: replichore length (nt).

_contract.summary: Initiate, elongate, and terminate replication forks: fire a round of replication when mass-per-oriC crosses the growth-rate-dependent critical threshold, extend forks by dNTP polymerization, and split domains into daughter chromosomes at the terminus.
_contract.description:
M_cell: cell mass (fg); n_oriC: oriC count; M_critical(τ): mass/oriC threshold at doubling time τ;
ν: stochastic elongation rate (nt/s); dt: timestep; L_replichore: replichore length (nt).

inputs.bulk: Reads counts of replisome trimer/monomer subunits and of the four dNTPs (and their PPi id) to gate initiation and cap elongation by the limiting dNTP.
inputs.active_replisomes: Reads each fork's domain_index, right_replichore flag, coordinates and massDiff_DNA to build the template sequences elongated this step.
inputs.oriCs: Reads the oriC count n_oriC (mass-per-origin trigger) and each oriC's domain_index to assign daughter domains on initiation.
inputs.chromosome_domains: Reads domain_index and child_domains to find the parent domains that carry an origin and to detect finished domains at termination.
inputs.full_chromosomes: Reads full-chromosome domain_index so a completed domain's chromosome can be re-pointed to a child domain and a second daughter chromosome added at termination.
inputs.listeners: Reads listeners.mass.cell_mass (M_cell) to compute mass per origin for the initiation test.
inputs.environment: Reads environment.media_id to look up the doubling time τ and thus the critical initiation mass M_critical for the current condition.
inputs.timestep: Reads dt to scale the elongation rate over the step.
inputs.global_time: Reads current simulation time to stamp a new full chromosome's division_time (global_time + D_period).

outputs.bulk: On initiation decrements 6 trimer + 2 monomer replisome subunits per oriC; during elongation subtracts dNTPs used and adds the equal count of PPi; on termination returns 3 trimer + 1 monomer subunits per deleted replisome.
outputs.active_replisomes: Adds two replisomes per oriC (one per replichore) at initiation, advances fork coordinates and adds Δm_DNA to massDiff_DNA during elongation, deletes both forks of a domain at termination.
outputs.oriCs: Re-assigns existing oriCs to new daughter domain indices and adds one new oriC per existing origin so each daughter keeps an origin.
outputs.chromosome_domains: Adds two child domains per origin (no children yet) and links them as children of the originating parent domain.
outputs.full_chromosomes: At termination re-points a finished chromosome to its first child domain and adds a second daughter full_chromosome, each with division_time = global_time + D_period.
outputs.listeners: Writes replication_data.critical_initiation_mass (M_critical, fg) and critical_mass_per_oriC (M_cell/n_oriC ÷ M_critical, dimensionless).

config.basal_elongation_rate: Basal replication-fork speed ν (nt/s) that make_elongation_rates draws around.
config.criticalInitiationMass: Fallback critical initiation mass (fg) when no media-specific value applies.
config.get_dna_critical_mass: Callable mapping the current doubling time τ to the critical initiation mass.
config.nutrientToDoublingTime: Map from media_id to doubling time τ, selecting M_critical for the condition.
config.make_elongation_rates: Callable producing per-fork stochastic elongation rates from the basal rate.
config.mechanistic_replisome: If True, initiation requires (and consumes) explicit replisome subunits; else forks assemble freely.
config.replichore_lengths: Per-replichore length L_replichore; a fork terminates when |coordinate| reaches it.
config.replisome_protein_mass: Protein mass (fg) added per replisome when mechanistic_replisome is on.
config.replisome_trimers_subunits: Bulk ids of the trimeric replisome subunits (6 per oriC consumed/assembled).
config.replisome_monomers_subunits: Bulk ids of the monomeric replisome subunits (2 per oriC consumed/assembled).
config.dntps: Bulk ids of the four dNTPs consumed during elongation.
config.ppi: Bulk id of pyrophosphate released per polymerized nucleotide.
config.polymerized_dntp_weights: Per-dNTP polymerized masses used to compute Δm_DNA per fork.
config.sequences: Template DNA sequences the forks polymerize against.
config.replication_coordinate: Genomic coordinates anchoring the replication templates (stored at init; unused in this build's update path).
config.D_period: C+D-period timer added to global_time to schedule division on a new full chromosome.
config.no_child_place_holder: Sentinel domain index marking a chromosome domain with no children yet.

math: 1. Initiation: fire when  M_cell / n_oriC ≥ M_critical(τ);  +2 replisomes·oriC, +2 domains.
2. Elongation: seqs = buildSequences(template, pos, ν·dt); polymerize(seqs, dNTPs, limit);
Δm_DNA = ∑ᵢ (elongated_ntᵢ · weightᵢ);  PPi released = dNTP polymerized.
3. Termination: fork ends when |coordinate| = L_replichore; domain splits, subunits recycled.

symbols.n_oriC: number of origins of replication (oriC) currently present (count)
symbols.M_critical: critical mass-per-oriC threshold for initiation (fg), a function of doubling time
symbols.\u03c4: doubling time set by the current media/nutrient condition (min)
symbols.\u03bd: stochastic per-fork elongation rate, nucleotides per second (nt/s)
symbols.L_replichore: replichore length; fork terminates when |coordinate| reaches it (nt)
symbols.\u0394m_DNA: DNA mass added to a fork from elongated nucleotides this step (fg)
symbols.PPi: pyrophosphate released, one per nucleotide polymerized (count)

assumptions: Initiation is synchronous across all origins in a step (no asynchronous firing); all oriCs fire together once M_cell/n_oriC ≥ M_critical.
With mechanistic_replisome on, a round fires only if the full 6 trimer + 2 monomer subunits per oriC are available.
Two replisomes are assembled per origin, one per replichore, sharing the origin's domain index.
Forks added this step are not elongated until the next step.
If one dNTP is limiting, all four are scaled by the same fractional limit to preserve stoichiometry; each nucleotide polymerized releases one PPi.
A domain splits into two daughter chromosomes only when both of its forks have reached the replichore length; released replisome subunits recycle to bulk.
dNTPs are consumed only by replication, so the process runs as a plain Step without partitioned allocation.

ecoli-polypeptide-initiation.doc:
Polypeptide Initiation — assembles 30S+50S → 70S ribosomes on mRNAs.

    n_inactive = min(n_30S, n_50S)                     (assemblable-ribosome pool)
    p_act = calculate_activation_prob(f, ν, lengths, p, dt)  (elongation/termination-rate balance targeting f)
    n_activate = int(p_act · n_inactive)               (ribosomes activated this tick)
    p_k = ηₖ·n_copiesₖ / ∑ⱼ ηⱼ·n_copiesⱼ                (per-monomer initiation prob)
    max_p = ν·dt / (footprint · n_activate);   overcrowded ⟺ p_k > max_p·n_copiesₖ → capped/rescaled
    n_new ~ Multinomial(n_activate, p);  each consumes one 30S + one 50S.
  f = media-dependent active fraction; ηₖ = translation efficiency; ν = ribosome elongation rate (aa/s).

_contract.summary: Assembles free 30S + 50S subunits into active 70S ribosomes on mRNAs. Takes an assemblable-ribosome pool n_inactive = min(free 30S, free 50S) and activates n_activate = int(p_act · n_inactive), where p_act = calculate_activation_prob(...) is an elongation-rate/termination-rate balance targeting the media-dependent active fraction f (active ribosomes are NOT read). The activated ribosomes are distributed across mRNAs by a translation-efficiency-weighted multinomial p_k, with a per-mRNA ribosome-footprint overcrowding probability cap.

inputs.environment: reads media_id to look up the media-dependent active-ribosome fraction f
inputs.listeners: reads ribosome_data.effective_elongation_rate from the previous tick to set the elongation rate ν used in the activation-probability / overcrowding calculation (falls back to media rate on tick 0)
inputs.RNA: reads mRNA unique molecules (TU_index, transcript_length, can_translate, is_full_transcript, unique_index) to compute per-cistron mRNA counts and assign newly-initiated ribosomes to specific transcripts
inputs.bulk: reads free 30S and 50S subunit counts; their minimum is the assemblable-ribosome pool n_inactive that bounds how many ribosomes can be activated
inputs.timestep: tick length dt (s), used in the activation-probability and max-p footprint calculation

outputs.bulk: decrements free 30S and 50S each by the number of ribosomes initiated
outputs.active_ribosome: adds one new 70S per initiation with protein_index, peptide_length=0, mRNA_index, and pos_on_mRNA at the cistron start
outputs.listeners: writes ribosome_data: did_initialize, per-monomer init events, target/actual translation probabilities, mRNA_is_overcrowded, max_p / max_p_per_protein, whether the activation count was reduced, and (poisson mode) the per-tick log-likelihood

config.active_ribosome_footprint_size: ribosome footprint on the transcript (nt), divided by 3 to an aa-length divisor; sets the max_p probability cap that flags a monomer's mRNA as overcrowded
config.active_ribosome_fraction: map media_id → target active-ribosome fraction f
config.translation_efficiencies: per-monomer translation efficiency ηₖ weighting the initiation probabilities
config.elongation_rates: map media_id → ribosome elongation rate; fallback rate feeding the activation-probability model
config.protein_lengths: per-protein length used to estimate translation time and expected termination in the activation-probability solve
config.cistron_to_monomer_mapping: index map from cistrons to protein monomers used to weight initiation probabilities
config.cistron_tu_mapping_matrix: sparse matrix mapping transcription-unit counts to cistron counts
config.variable_elongation: toggles per-protein variable elongation rates when building elongation rates
config.ribosome30S: bulk id of the 30S subunit consumed on initiation
config.ribosome50S: bulk id of the 50S subunit consumed on initiation
config.pdmp_initiation_mode: 'discrete' (legacy multinomial, Σ fixed to n_activate) or 'poisson' (independent per-monomer Poisson tau-leap, resource-capped by the inactive-ribosome pool)
config.polypeptide_init_prob_scale: poisson mode: scalar multiplying each per-protein initiation rate before Poisson sampling (1.0 = unperturbed)

math: n_inactive = min(n_30S, n_50S)                     (assemblable-ribosome pool)
p_act = calculate_activation_prob(f, ν, lengths, p, dt)  (elongation/termination-rate balance targeting f)
n_activate = int(p_act · n_inactive)               (ribosomes activated this tick)
p_k = ηₖ·n_copiesₖ / ∑ⱼ ηⱼ·n_copiesⱼ                (per-monomer initiation prob)
max_p = ν·dt / (footprint · n_activate);   overcrowded ⟺ p_k > max_p·n_copiesₖ → capped/rescaled
n_new ~ Multinomial(n_activate, p);  each consumes one 30S + one 50S.
f = media-dependent active fraction; ηₖ = translation efficiency; ν = ribosome elongation rate (aa/s).

symbols.n_inactive: assemblable-ribosome pool = min(n_30S, n_50S) — bounds how many ribosomes can be activated (count)
symbols.p_act: activation probability from calculate_activation_prob — an elongation-rate/expected-termination-rate balance that hits target fraction f (dimensionless, 0-1)
symbols.n_activate: ribosomes to activate this tick = int(p_act · n_inactive) (count)
symbols.\u03bd: ribosome elongation rate (aa/s) from the previous tick's effective rate (media fallback on tick 0), feeding p_act and max_p
symbols.\u03b7\u2096: translation efficiency of monomer k (dimensionless relative weight)
symbols.n_copies\u2096: cistron/transcript copy count of monomer k (count)
symbols.footprint: active-ribosome footprint size, default ≈24 nt (nt; divided by 3 → aa)
symbols.max_p: per-monomer maximum initiation probability from the footprint cap = ν·dt / (footprint · n_activate); overcrowded when p_k exceeds max_p·n_copiesₖ (dimensionless)

assumptions: 30S/50S subunits are consumed only by translation initiation — no other process competes, so it runs as a plain Step with no partitioning.
Each initiation consumes exactly one 30S and one 50S and starts the ribosome at peptide length 0.

A monomer's mRNA is overcrowded when its initiation probability p_k exceeds the footprint cap max_p·n_copiesₖ, where max_p = ν·dt / (footprint · n_activate); overcrowded probabilities are capped and rescaled onto the rest, or (if that cannot resolve it) the activation count n_activate is reduced. This is a probability cap, not a ribosome-spacing test — active ribosomes already on each mRNA are never counted.

ecoli-transcript-initiation.doc:
TranscriptInitiation — distributes activated RNAPs across TUs by weighted multinomial sampling.

    n_to_activate = round(f_active · n_total_RNAP) - n_active
    p_i = max(0, basal_prob_i + ∑_j delta_prob[i,j] · bound_TF_j)
    initiations ~ Multinomial(n_to_activate, p_i / ∑_i p_i)
  with p_i ← 0 for TUs that are footprint-crowded (~24 nt) or lack a chromosomal promoter.
  f_active: media-dependent active RNAP fraction;  delta_prob: sparse (COO→CSR) TF effect matrix.
  ppGpp (optional) modulates basal_prob and f_active via fitted functions.

_contract.summary: Activates inactive RNAPs and distributes them across transcription units by weighted multinomial (or Poisson tau-leap) sampling of per-promoter initiation probabilities.
_contract.description:
f_active: media-dependent active RNAP fraction;  delta_prob: sparse (COO→CSR) TF effect matrix.
ppGpp (optional) modulates basal_prob and f_active via fitted functions.

inputs.environment: reads media_id to select the media-dependent active-RNAP fraction f_active, the RNAP elongation rate, and the per-RNA-type (mRNA/tRNA/rRNA) synthesis-probability fractions for this tick.
inputs.full_chromosomes: presence gate: if the cell has no full chromosome, every promoter initiation probability is forced to zero (no initiation).
inputs.promoters: reads each promoter's TU_index and bound_TF to build the per-promoter probability p_i = basal_prob + delta_prob·bound_TF, and to map promoters↔transcription units.
inputs.bulk: reads the count of inactive RNAP (APORNAP-CPLX) to convert the activation probability into an integer number of RNAPs to activate.
inputs.timestep: reads the tick length to size the RNAP activation probability (_calculateActivationProb) and the footprint-crowding cap max_p.
inputs.ppgpp_state: reads optional basal_prob and frac_active_rnap written by PpgppInitiation; when present these override the media-default basal_prob and f_active and switch the TF effect to multiplicative.
inputs.dnaa_hydrolysis: reads promoter_fraction (bound fraction of dnaA-box sites) to scale down the dnaA TU's initiation probability (autoregulation).
inputs.RNAs: reads existing RNA unique molecules only to allocate fresh, non-colliding unique indices for the RNAs/RNAPs added this tick.

outputs.bulk: decrements the inactive-RNAP pool by the number of RNAPs activated.
outputs.RNAs: adds one partially-transcribed RNA unique molecule per initiation (transcript_length 0, linked to its RNAP via RNAP_index).
outputs.active_RNAPs: adds the newly activated RNAP unique molecules with starting coordinates, direction and domain index.
outputs.listeners: writes synthesis-probability diagnostics (target/actual rna_synth_prob, max_p, tu_is_overcrowded, total_rna_init), rRNA initiation counts, and rnap_data (did_initialize, rna_init_event, log_likelihood).

config.fracActiveRnapDict: media → active-RNAP fraction f_active lookup (media default when ppGpp regulation is off).
config.basal_prob: per-TU baseline synthesis probability vector basal_prob_i.
config.delta_prob: sparse COO TF-effect matrix (deltaV, deltaI, deltaJ, shape) on TU synthesis probabilities.
config.get_delta_prob_matrix: builds the dense delta_prob matrix (ppGpp-aware) at initialization.
config.rnaSynthProbFractions: media → target synthesis-probability fractions per RNA type (mRna/tRna/rRna) used to rescale p_i.
config.rnaSynthProbRProtein: media → fixed synthesis probabilities for ribosomal-protein TUs.
config.rnaSynthProbRnaPolymerase: media → fixed synthesis probabilities for RNAP-subunit TUs.
config.active_rnap_footprint_size: RNAP promoter footprint (~24 nt) that caps per-promoter init probability (max_p).
config.rnaPolymeraseElongationRateDict: media → RNAP elongation rate (nt/s); feeds the activation-probability and footprint cap.
config.rnaLengths: TU lengths (nt); set the expected transcription time and termination rate in the activation-probability calc.
config.idx_mRNA: TU indices classified as mRNA, for type-specific probability rescaling.
config.idx_rRNA: TU indices classified as rRNA, for type-specific probability rescaling.
config.idx_tRNA: TU indices classified as tRNA, for type-specific probability rescaling.
config.idx_rprotein: TU indices of ribosomal proteins, given fixed synthesis probabilities.
config.idx_rnap: TU indices of RNAP subunits, given fixed synthesis probabilities.
config.replication_coordinate: chromosomal coordinate per TU; set as the start coordinate of each new RNAP.
config.transcription_direction: per-TU transcription direction; set on each new RNAP.
config.ppgpp_regulation: whether ppGpp-dependent regulation is active (changes how the delta_prob matrix is built).
config.inactive_RNAP: bulk id of the inactive-RNAP (APORNAP-CPLX) pool drawn from.
config.variable_elongation: whether rRNA elongation rates are amplified when building elongation rates.
config.pdmp_initiation_mode: 'discrete' exact-sum multinomial vs 'poisson' per-promoter tau-leap sampling of initiations.
config.transcript_init_prob_scale: poisson mode: scalar multiplier on the per-promoter initiation rate before drawing Poisson samples (ABC-SMC knob).

math: n_to_activate = round(f_active · n_total_RNAP) - n_active
p_i = max(0, basal_prob_i + ∑_j delta_prob[i,j] · bound_TF_j)
initiations ~ Multinomial(n_to_activate, p_i / ∑_i p_i)
with p_i ← 0 for TUs that are footprint-crowded (~24 nt) or lack a chromosomal promoter.

symbols.n_to_activate: number of RNAPs to activate this tick (integer count)
symbols.p_i: initiation probability weight of transcription unit i (dimensionless)
symbols.basal_prob_i: baseline synthesis probability of TU i (dimensionless)
symbols.basal_prob: vector of baseline per-TU synthesis probabilities (dimensionless)
symbols.delta_prob[i,j]: additive effect of bound TF j on the synthesis probability of TU i (dimensionless)
symbols.bound_TF_j: 1 if TF j is bound at the promoter, else 0 (indicator)
symbols.ppGpp: guanosine tetraphosphate; its concentration modulates basal_prob and f_active (mol/L)

assumptions: Only TUs with at least one promoter on an existing chromosome can initiate; with no full chromosome no initiation occurs.
An RNAP occupies ~24 nt at the promoter; overcrowded TUs are capped at max_p and the excess probability mass is redistributed.
In discrete mode initiation events are a single multinomial draw so Σ initiations equals n_to_activate exactly; poisson mode gives independent per-promoter marginals with a resource cap.
rProtein and RNAP TUs carry fixed media-specific synthesis probabilities; remaining probability mass is rescaled around them.
TF effect is additive on basal_prob via the sparse delta_prob matrix; under ppGpp regulation it becomes multiplicative on the ppGpp-adjusted basal via a smooth accessibility gain b²/(b+K).

process-bigraph interface: Requesters read from all ports but only

_contract.summary: Partitioned process. calculate_request sizes RNA degradation from competitive Michaelis–Menten endoRNase kinetics (per-class stochastic draws distributed by saturation fraction fᵢ, bounded by supply) and reserves the RNAs, water and fragment bases needed; evolve_state applies endonucleolytic cleavage (Δfragments = S_endo·n_deg) then exonucleolytic digestion of fragment bases into NMPs.
_contract.description: [rᵢ]: RNA conc (mol/L); Kmᵢ: MM constant; νᵢ: endo flux; S_endo: cleavage stoich (NMP+PPi).

inputs.bulk: reads RNA counts, charged-tRNA counts (added to uncharged), endoRNase and exoRNase enzyme counts, fragment-base counts, and water; endo/exo counts and Kms set the degradation rates, and after partitioning the allocated RNA/water/fragment counts drive the reactions
inputs.RNAs: reads unique mRNA entries (TU_index, can_translate, is_full_transcript) to add translatable mRNAs to the degradation pool, deactivate cleaved mRNAs, and delete full inactive transcripts
inputs.listeners: reads mass.cell_mass to convert molecule counts to concentrations (V = cell_mass/cell_density) for the Michaelis–Menten rates
inputs.timestep: tick length dt (s) scaling the per-class degradation draws and the exoRNase capacity

outputs.listeners: writes rna_degradation_listener: per-cistron and (optionally) per-RNA degraded counts, nucleotides_from_degradation, fraction_active_endoRNases (∑fᵢ), diff_relative_first_order_decay, and fragment_bases_digested

config.Kms: per-RNA Michaelis–Menten constants Kmᵢ (mol/L), fitted to recapitulate first-order decay
config.kcat_exoRNase: exoRNase catalytic rate constant kcat_exo (1/s) setting exo digestion capacity
config.rna_deg_rates: first-order RNA degradation rates (1/s) used to report divergence from first-order decay
config.is_mRNA: boolean mask selecting mRNA-class RNAs (degraded as unique/deactivated)
config.degrade_misc: when true, degrade miscRNAs together with mRNAs (as one transient class)
config.cell_density: cell density ρ (g/L) converting cell_mass → volume for concentrations
config.n_avogadro: Avogadro constant N_A (1/mol) for counts↔concentration conversion
config.nt_counts: per-RNA nucleotide composition, forming the NMP rows of S_endo
config.rna_lengths: per-RNA length (nt) setting water needed for hydrolysis and total NMP yield
config.endoRNase_ids: bulk ids of endoRNases whose counts drive endonucleolytic flux
config.exoRNase_ids: bulk ids of exoRNases whose counts set exonucleolytic capacity
config.charged_trna_names: charged tRNA ids added to uncharged tRNA counts when sizing tRNA degradation
config.uncharged_trna_indexes: indices where charged-tRNA counts are folded into the RNA pool
config.cistron_tu_mapping_matrix: maps degraded transcription-unit counts to per-cistron degraded counts
config.polymerized_ntp_ids: fragment-base (polymerized NTP) ids produced by endo cleavage and digested by exo
config.nmp_ids: NMP ids produced by exonucleolytic digestion

math: fᵢ = ([rᵢ]/Kmᵢ) / (1 + ∑ⱼ [rⱼ]/Kmⱼ);   νᵢ = kcat_endo · [EndoRNase] · fᵢ
per class c: n_deg_c = Draw(∑_{i∈c} νᵢ · dt · V · N_A), multinomial∝fᵢ, ≤ supply
Δfragments = S_endo · n_deg;   exo: C_exo = ∑n_exo · kcat_exo · dt
FragmentBase + H2O → NMP + H⁺   (full digest if C_exo ≥ Σbases, else multinomial)

symbols.Km\u1d62: fitted Michaelis–Menten constant for RNA species i (mol/L)
symbols.f\u1d62: endoRNase saturation fraction for RNA i = ([rᵢ]/Kmᵢ)/(1+∑ⱼ[rⱼ]/Kmⱼ) (dimensionless)
symbols.\u03bd\u1d62: endonucleolytic degradation flux of RNA i = kcat_endo·[EndoRNase]·fᵢ
symbols.n_deg_c: total RNAs to degrade for class c ∈ {mRNA, tRNA, rRNA} (count)
symbols.n_deg: per-species vector of RNAs degraded this tick (count)
symbols.S_endo: endo cleavage stoichiometry matrix (metabolites × RNAs): NMP fragments + PPi
symbols.FragmentBase: polymerized nucleotide fragment released by endo cleavage
symbols.H2O: water consumed hydrolyzing fragment bases in exonucleolytic digestion (one per base; endonucleolytic cleavage consumes none) (count)
symbols.NMP: free nucleotide monophosphate released by exo digestion (count)
symbols.H\u207a: proton released per fragment base digested (count)

assumptions: Km values are fitted so the steady-state Michaelis–Menten rate recapitulates first-order RNA decay kd_i·r_i.
Bulk RNAs (tRNA/rRNA) are degraded immediately; unique mRNAs are deactivated on cleavage but not deleted until they are full transcripts, simplifying transcript elongation.

Cleaved RNA nucleotides are lumped as one linear chain of fragment bases (5' phosphate removed as PPi); exo digestion has no sequence specificity — one H2O consumed and one H⁺ released per base, and if C_exo ≥ total bases all fragments are digested, else a composition-weighted multinomial subsample.

ecoli-polypeptide-elongation_requester.doc:
Requester Step

Accepts a PartitionedProcess as an input, and runs in coordination with an
Evolver that uses the same PartitionedProcess.

process-bigraph interface: Requesters read from all ports but only
write to request, process, next_update_time, and optionally listeners.

_contract.summary: Partitioned process. calculate_request computes the ribosome elongation rate (model-specific: fixed/media-set, or ppGpp- and tRNA-charging-modulated in subclasses), builds the per-ribosome amino-acid sequences for the tick and requests the amino acids (and tRNAs/ATP for the charging model). evolve_state runs the polymerize algorithm over the allocated amino acids, advances peptide length and mRNA position, terminates finished ribosomes into 30S/50S + monomer, and reports GTP to hydrolyze.
_contract.description:
ν_eff ∝ min_a f_charged_a   (Michaelis–Menten competitive inhibition)
Charging (aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase): aa + ATP + tRNA → charged_tRNA + AMP + PPi.
Composes tRNA charging + ppGpp (RelA/SpoT) + amino-acid supply (synth/import/export).

inputs.environment: reads media_id to select the media-dependent basal ribosome elongation rate
inputs.listeners: reads mass.cell_mass and mass.dry_mass to convert counts to concentrations and to scale the amino-acid supply for the expected proteome doubling
inputs.active_ribosome: reads active ribosomes (protein_index, peptide_length, pos_on_mRNA) to build elongation sequences; writes back advanced lengths/positions/mass and deletes terminated ribosomes
inputs.bulk: reads and (post-allocation) consumes amino acids, tRNAs/ATP (charging model), water, and ppGpp reactants; produces finished protein monomers and released 30S/50S subunits
inputs.bulk_total: reads unpartitioned total counts (amino-acid pool sizes, enzyme/tRNA totals) for supply and concentration calculations
inputs.polypeptide_elongation: declared bidirectional process_state port; this process only WRITES it (gtp_to_hydrolyze, aa_count_diff, aa_exchange_rates carried to the metabolism process) — calculate_request/evolve_state never read it, so it is not an input in practice
inputs.timestep: tick length dt (s); elongation is capped at 22 aa/tick

outputs.bulk: consumes amino acids used (−aas_used); releases water per peptide bond formed (+nElongations − nInitialized, a condensation product); produces terminated protein monomers; and releases one 30S and one 50S per terminated ribosome (plus charging/ppGpp reactant changes in subclasses)
outputs.active_ribosome: advances peptide_length and pos_on_mRNA by the elongation achieved, adds incorporated-amino-acid mass, and deletes ribosomes that reached their protein's terminal length
outputs.listeners: writes ribosome_data (effective_elongation_rate read by polypeptide_initiation next tick, actual_elongations, termination stats, aa_counts) and growth_limits (aas_used, aa_allocated, net_charged, fraction_trna_charged, pool/request sizes)
outputs.polypeptide_elongation: writes gtp_to_hydrolyze (= gtpPerElongation·n_elongations) and aa_count_diff / aa_exchange_rates passed to metabolism

config.basal_elongation_rate: basal/maximum ribosome elongation rate ν (aa/s), ≈22; caps the media-scaled rate
config.ribosomeElongationRate: current ribosome elongation rate (aa/s), updated each tick from the model
config.ribosomeElongationRateDict: map media_id → basal elongation rate (aa/s) for the Base/Supply models
config.elongation_max: maximum elongation rate (aa/s) used as max_elong_rate in the tRNA-charging solve
config.variable_elongation: toggles per-protein variable elongation rates in make_elongation_rates and polymerize
config.gtpPerElongation: GTP hydrolyzed per amino acid (Base/Supply add +2 for charging removed from GAM; SteadyState uses the raw value)
config.translation_aa_supply: map media_id → per-mass amino-acid supply rate (mol/fg/min) capping the request in the Supply model
config.ppgpp_regulation: enable ppGpp-dependent modulation of the elongation rate and ppGpp turnover
config.disable_ppgpp_elongation_inhibition: when true, keep ppGpp metabolism but do not let ppGpp throttle the elongation rate
config.elong_rate_by_ppgpp: fitted function [ppGpp]→elongation rate (aa/s) evaluated when ppGpp inhibition is active
config.KD_RelA: RelA dissociation constant for the uncharged-tRNA activation term
config.k_SpoT_syn: SpoT basal ppGpp synthesis rate constant
config.kS: aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase charging rate constant (charging model)
config.KMaa: Michaelis constant for amino acids in the charging kinetics
config.KMtf: Michaelis constant for tRNA in the charging kinetics
config.krta: ribosome–charged-tRNA association constant in the elongation-rate solve
config.krtf: ribosome–free-tRNA constant in the elongation-rate solve
config.charging_stoich_matrix: stoichiometry of the tRNA charging reaction (aa+ATP+tRNA → charged_tRNA+AMP+PPi)
config.aa_from_trna: matrix projecting per-tRNA quantities onto a per-amino-acid basis
config.aa_from_synthetase: matrix projecting synthetase counts onto a per-amino-acid basis
config.mechanistic_translation_supply: use mechanistic (enzyme-based) amino-acid supply instead of the fitted proteome-doubling estimate
config.mechanistic_aa_transport: use mechanistic amino-acid import/export kinetics at the boundary
config.aa_supply_in_charging: include the amino-acid supply closure inside the tRNA-charging solve

math: f_charged_a = [charged_tRNA_a] / ([charged_tRNA_a] + [uncharged_tRNA_a])
ν_eff = effective elongation rate (aa/s); a indexes amino-acid species.

symbols.seqs: per-ribosome upcoming amino-acid sequences from buildSequences(protSeqs, ribo_pos, ν·dt)
symbols.\u0394len: per-ribosome peptide elongation achieved this tick = polymerize(seqs, aa, limit) (aa)
symbols.aa: free amino-acid counts available to the polymerize algorithm (count)
symbols.limit: polymerize resource limit (set large here; the real cap is handled in metabolism)
symbols.n_elongations: total amino-acid incorporation reactions this tick (count)
symbols.gtpPerElongation: GTP hydrolyzed per amino acid incorporated (≈4.2, EF-Tu/EF-G cycling)
symbols.GTP_consumed: total GTP to hydrolyze = n_elongations · gtpPerElongation (count)
symbols.ppGpp: guanosine tetraphosphate; its concentration throttles ν when regulation is on
symbols.RelA: ppGpp synthetase; synthesizes ppGpp from uncharged tRNA signal
symbols.SpoT: ppGpp hydrolase / basal synthetase (degradation + basal synthesis terms)
symbols.uncharged_tRNA: uncharged tRNA driving RelA-dependent ppGpp synthesis

assumptions: Elongation is capped at 22 aa per tick (the sequence matrix is padded with 22 PAD_VALUEs), so timesteps > 1 s under-count the effective rate.
One GTP-driven EF-Tu/EF-G cycle costs gtpPerElongation GTP per amino acid; GTP hydrolysis itself is charged in the metabolism process for growth-associated maintenance.
One water is released per peptide bond formed and none for the first residue of a newly initialized polypeptide.

The Base model requests exactly the amino acids implied by the upcoming sequence at max elongation and does not model tRNA charging (fraction_charged = 0); the TranslationSupply and SteadyState subclasses override the elongation-rate and amino-acid-count hooks (supply cap / charging-derived rate) but inherit this same contract.

ecoli-transcript-elongation_requester.doc:
Requester Step

Accepts a PartitionedProcess as an input, and runs in coordination with an
Evolver that uses the same PartitionedProcess.

process-bigraph interface: Requesters read from all ports but only
write to request, process, next_update_time, and optionally listeners.

_contract.summary: PartitionedProcess: calculate_request sizes the NTP request from the sequences each active RNAP could transcribe this tick; evolve_state polymerizes with the allocated NTPs, advances RNAP coordinates, terminates finished transcripts, and (optionally) attenuates tRNA operons.
_contract.description: early-terminated RNAPs recycled and partial transcripts discarded.

inputs.environment: reads media_id to select the media-dependent RNAP elongation rate ν used when building the transcribable sequences.
inputs.RNAs: reads TU_index, transcript_length and is_full_transcript of each partial RNA to build the sequences to elongate this tick.
inputs.active_RNAPs: reads each RNAP's coordinates, direction and unique_index to map RNAPs to their partial transcripts and advance their positions; an empty set short-circuits the tick.
inputs.bulk: reads available NTP (ATP/CTP/GTP/UTP) counts to bound the request (calculate_request) and the polymerization reaction limit (evolve_state).
inputs.bulk_total: reads total charged-tRNA counts (for attenuation) to convert to concentration when computing stop probabilities.
inputs.listeners: reads listeners.mass.cell_mass to form the counts→molar factor for the tRNA-attenuation stop-probability calculation.
inputs.attenuation_config: reads whether tRNA attenuation is enabled and its stop-probability function / attenuated-RNA indices / location lookup.

outputs.bulk: consumes NTPs, releases PPi (net = elongations − initiations, since the initiating nucleotide of each newly started transcript retains its 5′ triphosphate), returns inactive RNAP for terminated/attenuated/stalled RNAPs, and adds completed non-mRNA transcripts (and fragment bases if recycling stalls).
outputs.RNAs: sets updated transcript_length and mass submasses, marks completed transcripts as full, and deletes terminated non-mRNA / attenuated / stalled partial transcripts.
outputs.active_RNAPs: sets advanced coordinates and deletes RNAPs that terminated, attenuated, or (if enabled) stalled.
outputs.listeners: writes elongation diagnostics: count_rna_synthesized, count_NTPs_used, attenuation_probability/counts_attenuated, ntp pool/used, and rnap_data (actual_elongations, did_terminate, termination_loss, did_stall).

config.rnaPolymeraseElongationRateDict: media → RNAP elongation rate ν (nt/s) that sets how far each RNAP can move per tick.
config.rnaSequences: padded per-TU nucleotide-index sequences used by buildSequences/polymerize.
config.rnaLengths: annotated per-TU lengths (nt); termination fires when transcript_length reaches this.
config.ntWeights: per-nucleotide molecular weights wᵢ used to compute transcript mass increase.
config.endWeight: mass added once, when a transcript is first initiated (5′-end weight).
config.ntp_ids: bulk ids of the four NTPs consumed during elongation.
config.ppi: bulk id of inorganic pyrophosphate (PPi) released during elongation (net = elongations − transcript initiations).
config.inactive_RNAP: bulk id of the inactive-RNAP pool that terminated/attenuated/stalled RNAPs return to.
config.is_mRNA: per-TU mask; partial mRNAs stay as unique molecules on termination while other RNA types become bulk counts.
config.replichore_lengths: right/left replichore lengths (nt); wrap RNAP coordinates that cross the origin/terminus.
config.variable_elongation: whether per-position variable elongation rates (e.g. amplified rRNA) are used.
config.make_elongation_rates: builds the per-sequence elongation-rate array from the media rate and timestep.
config.recycle_stalled_elongation: whether RNAPs on NTP-limited (stalled) transcripts are recycled to the inactive pool with their bases returned.
config.get_attenuation_stop_probabilities: fitted function mapping charged-tRNA concentration to per-operon early-termination probability p_stop.
config.attenuated_rna_indices: TU indices eligible for tRNA-attenuation early termination.
config.fragmentBases: bulk ids of NTP fragments returned when a stalled transcript is discarded.

math: seqs = buildSequences(rnaSeqs, RNAP_pos, ν·dt);  Δlen = polymerize(seqs, NTP, limit)
NTP → NMP_incorporated + PPi;   Δmass = ∑ᵢ Δntᵢ·wᵢ  [fg]
Termination: transcript len = TU_len → full transcript; RNAP recycled.
tRNA attenuation (optional): p_stop = f([charged_tRNA]),
ν = elongation rate (nt/s); dt = timestep; wᵢ = nucleotide weights.

symbols.w\u1d62: molecular weight of nucleotide i (fg per molecule / g·mol⁻¹)
symbols.\u0394mass: transcript mass increase from elongation this tick (fg)
symbols.\u0394len: number of nucleotides added to a transcript this tick (nt)
symbols.p_stop: early-termination (attenuation) probability of an attenuated tRNA operon (dimensionless, 0–1)
symbols.NTP: ribonucleoside triphosphate consumed per elongation step (count)
symbols.PPi: inorganic pyrophosphate released during elongation, net of transcript-initiating nucleotides that retain their 5′ triphosphate (count)
symbols.charged_tRNA: absolute charged (aminoacylated) tRNA concentration passed directly to the attenuation stop-probability function f (mol/L)

assumptions: NTP pools are allocated across all active RNAPs by the polymerize algorithm to maximize total elongation subject to the available-NTP reaction limit.
An RNAP terminates exactly when its transcript_length reaches the annotated TU length.
Partial mRNAs are already functional and are kept as unique molecules; completed non-mRNA transcripts become bulk molecules.

tRNA attenuation is optional; when enabled, RNAPs stochastically terminate early with per-operon probability f([charged_tRNA]) — the fitted function of absolute charged-tRNA concentration, not a charged/total ratio — and their partial transcripts are discarded.
RNAP coordinates wrap at the replichore boundaries (origin/terminus).
